_comment: Phase 1201 plan 04 (D-16) table-driven parser conformance corpus. Read exclusively by DG/tests/DG.Tests/SwrlSubsetConformanceTests.cs -- see README.md in this directory. This corpus is separate from and additive to the frozen fixtures/golden/fixture.json (1200 D-11); it is NOT frozen the same way -- see README.md for what does and does not require a Change-Reason Log entry.

cases.description: A >=2-arg, non-swrlb: predicate resolved by a supplied resolver as an ObjectProperty parses to ObjectPropertyAtom (D-02, first reachable case) and the overall parse is a clean passed with no diagnostics.

The same adjacentTo(?a,?b) predicate parsed with the null-object resolver (no resolverConfig entries) cannot be resolved and yields UnsupportedAtom plus an unresolvable-predicate-kind diagnostic, rolling up to unsupported. This is the default behavior of Parse()/TryParse() with no resolver argument, and the second half of D-02 that must be locked down alongside the resolved case above.

An atom whose text does not match the required predicate(args) shape (here, an unbalanced/missing opening parenthesis) yields a typed non-verdict -- UnsupportedAtom plus an atom-regex-miss diagnostic -- never a thrown exception.
A quoted literal containing an embedded comma splits into the correct two-argument count, with the comma preserved inside the literal value rather than being treated as an argument separator.
A backslash-escaped quote embedded inside a quoted literal is unescaped rather than terminating the literal early or being left in the value verbatim.
An expression containing more than one '->' yields a typed error (arrow-arity) with no rule produced, never a thrown exception.

A quoted literal with an explicit ^^datatype suffix records that datatype verbatim (xsd:decimal) rather than re-inferring it from the lexical form (which would otherwise also infer xsd:decimal here, but the point is the explicit value is what is recorded -- see the language-literal case for a suffix that would otherwise be mis-inferred).

A quoted literal with an @lang suffix records the language tag and defaults its datatype to xsd:string, distinguishing it from the unsuffixed inference chain that would otherwise never set Language at all.

An unrecognized/malformed atom conjoined with a well-formed atom in the same body is emitted as UnsupportedAtom for the malformed atom while the surrounding well-formed atom is preserved intact (D-03: never dropped) -- the rule is still produced with both atoms present, one typed unsupported and one typed normally.
